interim_updates.company_name: HOUSING DEVELOPMENT FINANCE CORPORATION BANK OF SRI LANKA
interim_updates.note_text: HDFC Bank of Sri Lanka reported H1 2026 (six months ended 30 June 2026) Total Operating Income of Rs.1,499mn, down 2.35% YoY from Rs.1,535mn, as Net Interest Income fell to Rs.1,365mn from Rs.1,417mn (interest income fell faster than interest expense: Interest Income Rs.3,569mn vs Rs.3,736mn, Interest Expenses Rs.2,203mn vs Rs.2,319mn) even as Net Fee and Commission Income grew to Rs.133mn from Rs.119mn. Despite lower revenue, Profit Before Tax nearly doubled to Rs.205mn (+84.68% YoY, from Rs.111mn) and PAT grew to Rs.105mn from Rs.27mn (+288.89% YoY), aided materially by cost control (Personnel Expenses fell to Rs.805mn from Rs.893mn) and, importantly, by a net impairment WRITE-BACK (reversal) of Rs.83mn in H1 2026 versus a smaller Rs.39mn write-back in H1 2025 -- Impairment Charges are booked as a negative (income-boosting) figure in both periods, so this is a non-recurring, provision-release driven boost to profit rather than pure operating improvement, and the Rs.44mn YoY increase in the size of that reversal equals over 40% of the entire Rs.94mn YoY increase in PBT (Rs.205mn - Rs.111mn = Rs.94mn). For the quarter alone (Q2 2026 vs Q2 2025), the Bank swung from a Rs.4mn net loss to a Rs.34mn net profit, with the quarter's impairment line also a Rs.49mn write-back versus a Rs.35mn charge a year earlier -- the same provision-release dynamic evident quarter-on-quarter. Asset quality remains a structural concern: Impaired Loans (Stage 3) to Total Loans ratio (net basis) stood at 46.89% as at 30 June 2026 (47.04% at 31 Dec 2025) -- driven mainly by legacy EPF-related pawning/lending exposures, since the same ratio excluding EPF loans is a much lower 23.42% (net basis). Cost-to-Income ratio remains elevated at 78.10% (77.24% at 31 Dec 2025). Capital ratios are exceptionally strong and well above regulatory minimums (Total Capital Ratio 32.05% vs 12.5% minimum; CET1 29.98% vs 7.0% minimum), reflecting the Bank's small, low-leverage balance sheet (Total Assets Rs.63,187mn) rather than superior earnings generation.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is the first financial_statements entry for HDFC, so no prior quarter (e.g. Q1 2026 / 31 March 2026) is available for sequential comparison. Reporting basis: HDFC Bank of Sri Lanka is a single entity with no subsidiaries or associates disclosed in this filing (no Group columns presented), so only one GROUP-basis row is entered. Figures are in Rs. Millions per this filing's own presentation (unit_scale='Mn'), not thousands, and cannot be directly compared in magnitude to other banks entered this session without adjusting for scale. The filing provides both quarter-only and H1 cumulative columns for the Income Statement (Dec FYE bank) but the Statement of Cash Flows discloses only H1-cumulative figures, consistent with the H1 basis used here throughout.
interim_updates.takeaway: Headline PAT growth (+288.89% YoY) looks dramatic but is materially inflated by a larger impairment write-back (Rs.83mn H1 2026 vs Rs.39mn H1 2025, a Rs.44mn swing that alone accounts for roughly 47% of the Rs.94mn YoY increase in PBT) rather than organic revenue growth -- Total Operating Income actually fell 2.35% YoY as Net Interest Margin compressed (4.30% vs prior periods per the ratio table) on a shrinking net interest income base. The improvement is real at the bottom line but is a cost-control-and-provision-release story, not a revenue growth story, and the very high net Stage 3 impaired-loans ratio (46.89%, concentrated in EPF-related lending) remains the key balance-sheet risk to monitor even though capital ratios are comfortably above regulatory minimums.
operational_highlights: H1 2026 Total Operating Income Rs.1,499mn, down 2.35% YoY from Rs.1,535mn, on Net Interest Income of Rs.1,365mn (vs Rs.1,417mn) as both Interest Income and Interest Expenses declined YoY
H1 2026 PBT Rs.205mn (+84.68% YoY) and PAT Rs.105mn (+288.89% YoY); Q2 2026 alone swung from a Rs.4mn net loss (Q2 2025) to a Rs.34mn net profit
Net impairment WRITE-BACK of Rs.83mn in H1 2026 (vs a Rs.39mn write-back in H1 2025) -- a non-recurring, provision-release-driven boost equal to roughly 47% of the YoY increase in PBT
Personnel Expenses fell to Rs.805mn from Rs.893mn H1 YoY, the main organic driver of the profit improvement alongside the impairment release
Net Stage 3 Impaired Loans ratio 46.89% (47.04% at 31 Dec 2025) but only 23.42% excluding EPF-related loans -- asset quality concentrated in a specific legacy lending category

Capital ratios far above regulatory minimums: Total Capital Ratio 32.05% (12.5% minimum), CET1 29.98% (7.0% minimum), reflecting balance sheet size (Rs.63,187mn total assets) more than earnings strength
Cost-to-Income ratio 78.10% (77.24% at 31 Dec 2025), still elevated for a licensed bank
key_drivers: Impairment Charges line reversed to a Rs.83mn net write-back in H1 2026 from a Rs.39mn write-back in H1 2025 (both periods show provision releases, but the release grew Rs.44mn YoY) -- flagged as the single largest identifiable non-recurring contributor to the PBT increase, per the Income Statement's own Impairment Charges line (Rs.(83)mn H1 2026 vs Rs.(39)mn H1 2025)

Net Interest Income fell to Rs.1,365mn from Rs.1,417mn H1 YoY as Interest Income (Rs.3,569mn to Rs.3,736mn) declined faster than Interest Expenses could be cut (Rs.2,203mn to Rs.2,319mn) -- a genuine revenue headwind masked by the impairment release and cost cuts below the line
Personnel Expenses cut to Rs.805mn from Rs.893mn H1 YoY (-9.86%) is the clearest organic (non-provision) profit driver, alongside a reduction in Other Expenses (Rs.287mn from Rs.290mn)
Net Fee and Commission Income grew to Rs.133mn from Rs.119mn H1 YoY (+11.76%), a genuine bright spot but too small in absolute terms (Rs.14mn) to offset the Rs.52mn Net Interest Income decline
